title: PI plan — tranche 9 (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
body:
# PI plan — tranche 9

## Objectives

- **O1 — S20 is accepted and its closure is placed.** The eval hillclimb is reworked against its record and closed through its closure gate with a published closure review, so the tranche's only P0 package (`project_in_unauthorised_tranche:S20`, cleared by authorisation) and its two closure P1s leave the register together.
- **O2 — S21 is accepted on evidence, not construction.** The compiled-prompt slice is built (all nine linked issues closed); this tranche supplies its charter, artefacts, registers, contract and Phase-G review, and its receipt is green with the project still active.
- **O3 — S18 is reworked to a settled record.** The kata improvement loop's slice is authored to the standard, its WBS deliverable carries the plan's WSJF, and its receipt is green with the project still active because issue #12 remains open.
- **O4 — the tranche exits on evidence.** Three fresh receipts at one snapshot sha and a green `check-tranche-exit`, so the tranche-9 review #755 reads a measured tranche and not a claim.

## Plan

The three members are reworked by the retrospective factory against the same replay record, one pack each, in the order the tranche's refinement records. Readiness (four cadences, the PI documents, the plan approval and the retro lesson) is written first because two tranche-scope P1 packages are due the moment the tranche is authorised, and every member's `pi_cadence`, `pi_plan`, `pi_objectives` and `lessons` checks read it.

The execution order is WSJF order: S20, then S21, then S18. The factory's own roster is sorted by project key (S18, S20, S21) and is not rewritten to match: the two orders answer different questions, and the refinement is the re-estimate of record.

## WSJF order

| rank | member | business value | time criticality | risk reduction | job size | WSJF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | S20 | 7 | 5 | 6 | 5 | 3.60 |
| 2 | S21 | 9 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 2.75 |
| 3 | S18 | 9 | 6 | 9 | 13 | 1.85 |

S20 ranks first because it is the smallest job and carries the only P0 and the closure set; S21's product is already built and its delay cost is carried by the audit, not by construction; S18 is the largest job and declares S13 and S15 as dependencies, both of which deliver in tranches 8 and 7.

## Capacity and WIP

- One live record writer: the replay record is shared with the tranche-7 and tranche-8 lanes, so the tranche-9 rows are written by one session at a time and only at `period='tranche-9'`.
- One factory invocation: `rework-batch.py` is serial and refuses a dirty lane; the tranche-9 journal (`docs/evidence/rework/batch/tranche-9.jsonl`) is its single lock.
- WIP limits: two open batches and one open card per writer. S20 is cleared first so its closure gate is not competing with a second member's cards.
- Read agents: at most six, and no second full test suite on this box while a record write is in flight.

## Evidence

The packs are preflighted by `scripts/rework-content-check.py` at one pinned snapshot, each with its refinement WSJF and its computed `--closes` (false for S18 and S21, true for S20). The receipts are rendered by `scripts/verify-project.py` and the exit by `scripts/check-tranche-exit.py`; the readiness gate records the snapshot path, its sha and the three checker results. The register this work answers is `docs/evidence/rework-register.json`, whose 37 open packages touch this tranche.

## Dependencies

- **#755** — the tranche-8 review is the only writer of tranche 9's authorisation; the dry run and every receipt wait for it.
- **#951** — tranche 7 delivers S15, a declared dependency of S18 and S21.
- **#952** — tranche 8 delivers S13, a declared dependency of S18 and S21.
- **#12** — S18's open construction lane; this tranche neither closes it nor touches its branch.
- **#31** — S19's Tier-3 lane, S20's dependency's lane, not this tranche's to touch.

## Backlog refinement

The refinement re-estimates each member by its open package count rather than its slice prose: S20 13 (1 P0, 4 P1, 8 P2), S18 11 (3 P1, 8 P2), S21 11 (3 P1, 8 P2). It reorders the seed's membership (S18, S20, S21) to S20, S21, S18 for the reasons in the WSJF order, and it records the four integers of each member as the PI's re-estimate of record, which the batch reads before the first pack is preflighted.

The two tranche-scope packages `pi_cadence_missing:tranche-9` and `backlog_refinement_missing:tranche-9` are the refinement's own discharge: they clear when these rows and this record exist, and they are the reason the readiness step precedes every pack.
